solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Piano in bossa nova style? Arrangement of music secures band’s last award for sales (8,4)

indicatorNotes.Arrangement of: a musical arrangement reorders notes; here it reorders the letters of 'music'
indicatorNotes.secures: the rearranged letters hold the D inside them
indicatorNotes.last: takes only the final letter of 'band's'

blocks.note: p = piano, the musical marking for soft
bossa nova is a Brazilian, so Latin, style of music
rearranged, then split UM…ISC around the D
the final letter of 'band'

annotation.surface: A record review: a piano-led bossa nova track whose arrangement wins the band a sales award.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'bossa nova style' closes the first half; LATIN is the style, not a rhythm to anagram. The rest builds DISC's companion letters around one D.
annotation.definitionFit: A platinum disc is the award a record gets for reaching a set level of sales.

entries.clue: Weariness leads us carelessly to accept it (9)

indicatorNotes.carelessly: letters thrown down carelessly end up in a new order
indicatorNotes.to accept: the rearranged letters take IT in

blocks.note: LEADS US rearranged, split LASS…UDE
used as it stands, placed inside

annotation.surface: A tired guide lets the group drift along, accepting whatever comes.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay letters sit in plain sight: 'leads us' is the whole of the fodder, with 'it' tucked in.
annotation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, a lack of energy.

entries.clue: Row of houses excellent after town’s initial blunder (7)

indicatorNotes.initial: takes only the first letter of 'town's'
indicatorNotes.after: ACE follows the T and ERR

blocks.note: first letter of 'town'
to err is to blunder
ace = excellent

annotation.surface: Something about a fine row of houses built after a town planning mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Excellent after' puts the excellent part last, so the clue's word order is not the answer's order.
annotation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses joined side by side.

entries.clue: Metal prison cell’s centre (6)

indicatorNotes.centre: takes the two middle letters of 'cell'

blocks.note: the nick is British slang for prison or a police station
the middle two letters of CELL

annotation.surface: The metal bars at the heart of a prison cell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Metal prison cell' reads as one phrase about bars; the definition is only the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Nickel is a silvery metallic element.

entries.clue: I am repeatedly upset about impressionist (5)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: 'repeatedly' means again and again, so I AM is written out twice in a row
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: I'M written twice, then turned round to MIMI
c = circa, about

annotation.surface: Someone keeps getting upset about an impressionist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'upset about', but it has its own job as C, the abbreviation of circa.
annotation.definitionFit: A mimic is someone who imitates others, as an impressionist does.

entries.clue: Reserve that is seen around clubs (3)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so the letters of 'that is' encircle the C

blocks.note: i.e. = id est, that is
surface padding: it makes the sentence read naturally and supplies no letters
C = clubs, the card suit

annotation.surface: A reserve player seen hanging around the clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' is a noun meaning coolness of manner, not a substitute player.
annotation.definitionFit: Ice can mean cold reserve, as in an icy manner.

entries.clue: Chopped-up pear surrounded by cold cheese (10)

indicatorNotes.Chopped-up: a chopped pear is cut into pieces; its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.surrounded by: CHILLY closes round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: chilly = cold, split C…HILLY
PEAR rearranged, placed after the C

annotation.surface: A cheeseboard: chopped pear served with a cold cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a crumbly white cheese from Wales. 'Cold' looks like it describes the cheese but gives CHILLY.
annotation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a mild, crumbly Welsh cheese.

entries.clue: Employer returned CV after dismissing me (4)

indicatorNotes.returned: RESUME is sent back, read right to left
indicatorNotes.dismissing: ME is let go from the result

blocks.note: a CV is a résumé; RESUME turned round
ME is removed from the front of EMUSER

annotation.surface: An employer sends back a CV after firing the applicant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Employer' means one who employs something, a user, not a boss. The surface of hiring and firing is the misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a thing uses it, so an employer is a user.

entries.clue: Contend company favoured blocking the writer (7)

indicatorNotes.blocking: PET sits in the middle of ME, blocking it

blocks.note: Co. = company
the writer = the person writing, me; split M…E
a pet project is a favoured one

annotation.surface: A rival favoured by a company stands in the writer's way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter referring to themself, which gives ME.
annotation.definitionFit: To contend is to compete, to strive against rivals.

entries.clue: Paid out for church, no longer a major influence (5,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the person or thing; the answer names it

blocks.note: money paid out is spent
used as it stands
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: Money handed over to a church that no longer holds sway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' does double duty in the surface as a preposition but here simply supplies its own letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A spent force is someone or something that once had power but no longer does.

entries.clue: Bishop, pawn then rook? I end chess game (7)

blocks.note: P = pawn in chess notation
surface padding: it only sets the order of the pieces
R = rook in chess notation
used as it stands
checkmate ends a game of chess

annotation.surface: A chess player lists the pieces moved before announcing the winning finish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' sits among the chess pieces as if it were one of them, but it is the definition: a senior bishop in the church.
annotation.definitionFit: A primate is the chief bishop of a province or country, such as an archbishop.

entries.clue: Ape: copper returning to apprehend him (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: 'returning' means going back, so PC is read from its far end
indicatorNotes.to apprehend: CP catches HIM between its letters

blocks.note: PC = police constable; turned round to CP
used as it stands, held inside

annotation.surface: A police officer comes back to arrest a man, who is called an ape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the policeman, not the metal Cu, which fits the arrest story.
annotation.definitionFit: Chimp is the everyday short form of chimpanzee, one of the great apes.

entries.clue: What can be considered bliss? Exotic region can (9)

indicatorNotes.Exotic: exotic means strange and foreign; the letters take on an unfamiliar form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A holiday brochure asks what counts as bliss and answers that an exotic region can.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'ignorance is bliss'. The surface answer, an exotic region, is the false lead.
annotation.definitionFit: The proverb 'ignorance is bliss' says not knowing can be a happy state.

entries.clue: Loathing new articles about function (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the two articles go around USE

blocks.note: N = new
A and A, two indefinite articles; split A…A
a thing's function is its use

annotation.surface: Someone dreads fresh paperwork about what a thing is for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' means grammatical articles, here two copies of A.
annotation.definitionFit: Nausea can mean strong disgust or loathing as well as sickness.

entries.clue: British and French article I state (6)

blocks.note: Br = British
une = the feminine French for a
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A British and French writer declares his position in an article.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I state' reads as someone declaring something; 'state' is the definition, a country.
annotation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate, a state on the island of Borneo.

entries.clue: Runs tavern in centre? Nonsense (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the tavern sits within the centre

blocks.note: R = runs, from cricket scoring
a hub is a centre; split HU…B
a bar is a tavern

annotation.surface: Someone runs a pub in the town centre, and someone else scoffs at the idea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' is British slang for nonsense, and also what actors mutter to sound like background chatter.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is informal British English for nonsense or rubbish.

entries.clue: Name of encryption device deployed in game (6)

indicatorNotes.deployed: the letters are sent out into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: A wartime code machine used as part of a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the setting but is part of the fodder. Enigma was the German cipher machine of the Second World War.
annotation.definitionFit: Enigma is the name of the German cipher machine cracked at Bletchley Park.

entries.clue: Deal with all competitors in competition (5)

blocks.note: a verb: to handle a question from the floor, or stop a ball in cricket
a noun: the whole set of entrants lining up for a race

annotation.surface: An organiser handling everyone who has entered a contest.
annotation.walkthrough: To field a question is to deal with it; the field is everyone taking part in a race or contest.
annotation.definitionFit: You field a query when you deal with it, and the field is the whole set of entrants.

entries.clue: Graciously agree to plan, if son is excluded (5)

indicatorNotes.is excluded: the S is left out of DESIGN

blocks.note: a design is a plan
S = son, removed from DESIGN

annotation.surface: A parent agrees to a plan, on condition their son is left out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' links the definition to the wordplay; 'if' merely sets the condition in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Deign carries a note of condescension: you agree, but as a favour from above.

entries.clue: Indifferent regarding nerves, getting tense inside (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' means within, so T is placed within the word for nerves

blocks.note: neural = relating to nerves; split NEU…RAL
T = tense, as in grammar

annotation.surface: Someone claims not to care about nerves while feeling tense inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' sounds like nervousness in the surface but is the grammar abbreviation T.
annotation.definitionFit: Neutral means taking no side, indifferent between options.

entries.clue: Impression obtained from church possibly causing friction (7)

blocks.note: a copy of a church memorial brass, made by pressing wax over paper laid on it
a verb form: two surfaces moving against each other make friction

annotation.surface: A church visit that stirs up trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: A brass rubbing is an impression of a church brass made by rubbing wax over paper laid on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A rubbing is a copied impression, and rubbing is what causes friction.

entries.clue: Ask English in Great Britain to rise up (3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means contained by, so E is held by the letters of Great Britain
indicatorNotes.to rise up: in a down clue, the letters read upward

blocks.note: E = English
GB = Great Britain; G(E)B then read upward

annotation.surface: A plea for the English in Britain to stage an uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To rise up' is written for a down entry, where the letters read from bottom to top.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to beg is to ask, usually earnestly or humbly.

entries.clue: Pleasure trip abandoned by Jack and relative (4)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: 'abandoned by' means deserted, so the jack walks out of the trip and leaves the rest

blocks.note: a jaunt is a short pleasure trip
J = jack, the card; removed from JAUNT

annotation.surface: A day out that Jack and a relative both skipped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a person in the surface but is J from a pack of cards.
annotation.definitionFit: An example of the general term: an aunt is one kind of relative.

entries.clue: Enlarge limbs after recasting controversial sculptures (5,7)

indicatorNotes.after recasting: recasting reshapes a sculpture; here it reshapes the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A sculptor makes the limbs bigger when recasting some disputed statues.
annotation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are Parthenon sculptures taken to Britain by Lord Elgin and kept in the British Museum; Greece wants them back.
annotation.definitionFit: The Elgin Marbles are sculptures whose ownership Greece and Britain have long disputed.
